Charter Primary School Wood Lane, Chippenham Wiltshire, SN15 3EA Telephone: 01249 447 223 admin@charter.wilts.sch.uk Twitter @CharterPrimary
Headteachers Welcome
There is always something happening at Charter Primary School, whether it’s enjoying one of our Family learning events, learning new languages or supporting our many sports clubs. We have tried to convey some of that sense of both wonder and celebration through this site and allow you to see why our school means so much to us all.
The main aim of the school is to help our children to fulfill their potential in all areas of development and to grow into happy, effective, caring adults irrespective of background, ability or gender. We aim to offer a full and interesting curriculum encompassing knowledge, skills and understanding that will help prepare our children for future education and give them the skills and the enthusiasm to pursue learning for the rest of their lives.
We firmly believe in a genuine partnership between home and school. We all want the best for our children and it is only when this partnership is thriving that children flourish in our care. We always welcome parents into school, you are as important to us as your children – it is our school for the benefit of our children, and we hope that your association with the school is a long and happy one.
We warmly invite prospective parents to visit our school. If you would like to come and look around and catch a glimpse of what we get up to at Charter Primary School, please telephone the school office to make an appointment.
Mrs Sarah Flack Headteacher

British Values
Promoting British Values
As a school, we value and celebrate the diverse heritages of everybody at Charter. Alongside this, we value and celebrate being part of Britain. In general terms, this means that we celebrate traditions and customs in the course of the year; for example, Harvest Festival during the Autumn term and a Christmas Carol concert in St Andrews Church. We also value and celebrate national focusses, recent examples being; Universal Children’s Day and Safer Internet Day, with many more opportunities planned in throughout the year to collaborate with the wider community and world e.g. World Toilet Day. On a weekly basis, we use Picture News for one of our whole school assemblies which addresses different situations, linking to British Values & Rights Respecting. Our PSHE curriculum is categorised into key areas: Family and relationships, Wellbeing, Health, Safety, Citizenship & Economic wellbeing and supports how British Values are in intrinsic part of our curriculum.
At Charter Primary School, we teach the fundamental British Values explicitly through our PSHEE and RE curriculums as well as promoting these values through our ethos, the whole curriculum and our Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural development.
At Charter Primary School, we will actively challenge pupils, staff, parents or anyone in the school community expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British Values, including ‘extremist’ views.

Early Risers Breakfast Club
We offer sessions from 8am – 8.45am every day during term time at a cost of £6.00 per session, per child. This includes a light snack of toast and fruit juice. Drop in sessions are available on request at a cost of £6.50 per session.

Parent Helpers
Children love to have their parents – or grandparents – ‘helping’ at school and we love it too!
By having such volunteers, it lets the teaching staff plan smaller work groups and introduces a different set of skills and experiences to the classroom. Sometimes it’s a case of listening to the children read, other times it’s about encouraging them to solve problems or learn something new.
It’s not a huge commitment – as you can choose when to come in – but it is a commitment: your child will look forward to it and we will plan around having your help.
Please talk to your class teacher if you are able to help on a regular basis and complete a helper sheet for you to note the dates when you are coming in to help. You will be required to obtain a DBS (Disclosure & Barring Service) check and complete a volunteer training session which will include safeguarding training.
If helping in the classroom is not an option, then you can get involved in other ways. Being a School Governor is a great way to support the entire school and can be a good way to get to know how the school ticks as well as making a positive contribution. Elections are held as vacancies arise. Find out more on the Governor Page.
The other way in which you can help, is by getting involved in our fundraising activities. Many get involved with the CSFA (Charter School Friends Association) and raise fantastic sums of money for the school and have a great deal of fun in the process.
Parents and Carers Practical Working Group
A Parents and Carers Practical Working Group was introduced at Charter Primary School in Early 2019 with the aim of identifying tasks around the school site that adults and children could undertake to maintain and improve our lovely spaces. It also provides an opportunity for parents and children to socialise and work together.
Work has been undertaken so far to re-plant our bedding areas, re-store the bug hotel, paint the picket fence at the front of the school and paint the KS1 wall to allow children in our Resource Base to continue their learning outside.
We will be continuing the work of the Parents and Carers Practical Working Group this academic year and are always looking for volunteers to join us. Please contact the school office if you would like to express your interest in joining; either with planning, practical help or both.
Please view the photo gallery below to see some of the work that has taken place so far.

Rights Respecting
Everyone at Charter is proud to use the principles of UNICEF Rights Respecting. This means that we recognise that the rights of all children are at the centre of a healthy learning environment. Adults and children throughout the school community strive to ensure that all children, both in school and around the world, access their rights to the full.
All pupils learn about rights in lessons; pupils learn through rights by being encouraged to question, think critically, and challenge unfairness; and all classes act for rights by campaigning and advocating for the rights of children in the UK and abroad.
At Charter, the child is at the centre of everything we do.
Charter School Vision
Our ethos of Create, Discover, Succeed, Together supports the culture of Rights Respecting. The rights respecting values underpin all actions taken by leadership and management and that what is in the best interests of the child is of top priority. The whole school community learn about the rights of the child. This shared understanding helps us work together for global understanding and positive living. Charter school staff collaborate to develop and maintain a rights respecting community in all areas of school life. We are empowering our children through C,D,S,T to become active citizens and learners, with every child being able to say what they think in all matters affecting them and have their views taken seriously. All are encouraged to take an active role in their own learning and to speak and act for all to be respected.
Summary of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)
Click here to view a summary of the UN convention on the rights of the children.
Rights Respecting Discs
We created Rights Respecting discs that have been situated around the school, all of which represent some of the Unicef Rights Respecting Articles.
Charter children helped to decorate 4 discs during a ‘Learn with your Charter Child’ morning.
We hope that you enjoy looking at the finished discs when you come into the school.
Campaigning for a Better World
We believe that all children should participate in campaigning for a better world, fundraising for those in need, and also recognising when a person or organisation has gone over and above.
Since 2019 each class has made the commitment to sponsor a class elephant through the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust.
We collect glasses to be donated to World Vision through Spec Savers.
We have supported the charity ‘Smalls for All’ which provides underwear and hygiene kits for people in poverty and those who have been displaced by famine or war. Please click here to visit the Smalls for All website for further information.
We have donated to ‘Oxfam’ to supporting the following areas:
Access to clean water, Providing beginner bee kits to support making work fairer for women across the world, Way to Grow – Sustainable farming, Training and support women looking for work and starting their own businesses.
Linked to our World Book Day activities we are also supporting ‘Ryan’s Well’ foundation. Please click here to visit the Ryan’s Well website for further information.
Events can be followed on the class Twitter pages.

Children’s Leadership Team
Child leadership programme
Here at Charter, we want our pupils to be fully involved in their school. This involves the children taking on roles of responsibility and having a say on how we do things.
Each year group has a specific responsibility as follows:
Year 1: Assembly door monitors
Year 2: Eco-Warriors
Year 3: Ping’s Pals (Play leaders)
Year 5: Charity ambassadors
Year 6: Subject ambassadors
Headteacher and Deputy Headteacher Ambassadors
There are 2 nominated head teacher ambassadors who support the head teacher and 2 nominated deputy head teacher ambassadors who support the deputy head by:
Showing visitors around school
Hosting lunch for invited guests
Being involved in celebration assemblies
Subject Ambassadors
All children in year 6 are subject ambassadors and support the Subject Lead teacher with pupil voice, sharing ideas and running subject assemblies.
School Council
The school council group are led and run by the Headteacher and Deputy Headteacher Ambassadors. Children from each year group, share ideas and gain other children’s opinions on different topics such as school lunches and OPAL.

Woodlands Nursery
We are a long standing small caring, friendly, parent committee run charity Pre-school.
Woodlands Pre-school is registered with Ofsted, able to take Children from ages 2 – 5 . We are a member of the Pre-school learning Alliance and have comprehensive insurance with them.
We moved to Charter Primary School in September 2008, with a new management highly dedicated to providing quality and affordable sessional day care for families in the local area. We provide a happy, secure enviornment where children can meet their full potential. Woodlands Pre-school is based in a self contained annexe of Charter Primary School, which has been renovated to very high standards. We have a secure enclosed playground with the opportunity to use the school playgrounds, fields and multi-purpose sports area, which we can for a variety of outdoor activities.
Woodlands Pre-school is open Monday to Friday 9.00am to 3pm. We accept children aged 2 to 5. We accept Nursery Education Grant. As from September 2013, Woodlands Pre-School is able to accept funding avalible for 2 year olds.
At Woodlands Pre-school we believe in providing happy, caring and safe surroundings where your child can progress and thrive in a friendly and constructive enviornment. We strive to give your child a flying start by encouraging individual development, hand in hand with helping every child to socialise and gain confidence ready for their future lives.
The Manager at Woodlands Pre-School is qualified at a level 4 N.V.Q, and all other members of staff are qualified at N.V.Q Level 2 or higher. All staff are First Aid trained and CRB checked. We ensure all staff attend regular in service training with recognised bodies to extend knowledge and experience.
Children with additonal needs are welcome at Woodlands Pre-school. The setting has a SENCO co-ordinator who is also qualified at Level 4 in this area. Please feel free to come and discuss your child’s individual needs.
Please contact Sarah Ferris for more details on 01249 447578.

S’Cool Kids After School Club
New in September 2019, Charter’s S’Cool Kids After School Club.
We currently offer sessions from 3.15 – 4.15pm every day during term time at a cost of £6.00 per session, per child. This includes a light snack of toast and fruit juice. Drop in sessions are available on request at a cost of £6.50 per session.
Activities for the children to enjoy include indoor P.E equipment, outdoor climbing equipment, access to the ICT suite, arts and crafts and many more.
Details of our terms and conditions can be found under forms on our WEDUC parent app, or a paper copy can also be available on request.
If you are interested in the S’Cool Kids after school club and would like further details please contact the school office.

Early Years
On this page you will find lots of information about our Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and what happens in our EYFS class when your child starts at Charter School.
Under the Getting Ready to Start School section, you will find some helpful information and tips on how you can support your child before they start school.
Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any queries.
What happens in our EYFS class at Charter?
We aim to inspire and excite children to want to learn more. The Early Years Foundation is where our children begin their learning journey at Charter and where we endeavour to develop an understanding of the rights that all children should enjoy. It is the foundation in which everything else is built and so it is crucial to foster a love of learning from the offset.
Children learn best through play and active learning. We wish to help nurture a ‘can have a go’ attitude in our children, encourage risk taking within an environment that supports the growth of happy children.
Learning is achieved through a well-balanced range of both child and adult led learning opportunities in both the classroom and our outdoor environment. We are guided by your children. Through observations of child led play, adults can then plan and provide the next steps in your child’s unique learning journey.
Through the EYFS we aim to develop the principles of learning through the 7 areas of learning and development alongside the 3 learning characteristics as set out below:

Reading in Early Years
Reading unlocks so many doors for us all and therefore we are passionate about teaching all our children to read. It helps develop not only their vocabulary but also their imagination, spelling and enriches their lives.
Children have access to a range of reading materials. Our children take home a reading book matched to their phonic stage of development as well as additional reading books that can be read with their parents. This gives them the opportunities to practise their own reading skills and apply the phonics that they are learning each week as well as hear stories read to them. The additional reading books give them exposure to a range of keywords and texts with varying features.
All our children visit our school library. Here they can look at the covers, take a look inside books and pick one that really takes their fancy!
All reading is valuable so we encourage parents to record comments of books that they enjoy reading with their children at home on our home learning platform. We love seeing what stories the children are enjoying at home.
Hearing stories read is all part of developing a love of reading amongst our children so daily class stories are treasured. All of the adults in our Early Years class share books with the children and we even have some of our older children read stories to the whole class or as 1-to-1 ‘buddy’ reading. Our Year 1 children thoroughly enjoy being whole class readers!
Phonics in Early Years
At Charter School, we follow Read Write Inc to teach phonics. It is a whole-school approach to phonics that provides comprehension, handwriting, spelling and composition to get your children reading, writing and speaking fluently.
Please click here to view more information about how we teach phonics at Charter.
